title: macOS Automator workflow on selected text stopped working in Firefox 111.0 release
body: I use a macOS Automator workflow that translates selected text. It stopped working in Firefox 111.0: invoking the service on selected text now shows an error saying the service could not be used. Expected: the selected text is supplied to the workflow, which opens a Safari popup with the translation. Screenshot of the error attached.

symptoms_visible: Invoking the Automator selected-text service from Firefox 111.0 fails with 'service could not be used'; the workflow previously opened a translation popup with the selected text.
N0.label: N0 service error reported

symptoms_visible: I went through the macOS privacy settings and found no permission toggle for Firefox that applies to this service; the linked article is about third-party Automator actions, which my workflow doesn't use. The error is unchanged.
N1_x.label: N1_x permission-regrant aftermath

symptoms_visible: The service error still occurs in Firefox 111; the same workflow works in other applications and worked in earlier Firefox versions.
N2.label: N2 regression established

symptoms_visible: The service error still occurs on the installed release build; URL-based selected-text workflows fail the same way.
N3.label: N3 regressor bisected

symptoms_visible: The provided try build (target.dmg) runs the workflow correctly on both of our machines; the installed release build still shows the error.
N4.label: N4 fix verified on try build

symptoms_visible: The Automator workflow works again on builds containing the fix; the 'service could not be used' error no longer appears.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Treat it as a macOS permissions problem after an OS update: re-grant Firefox the relevant service permissions in System Settings.
solution.concrete_example: Have you had a recent macOS update? You may have to grant permissions (again) in System Settings — see the linked article about enabling Automator actions.

edges.comment: Real thread c2-c5: no applicable permission toggle exists; the linked article covers third-party Automator actions the workflow does not use; direction falsified.

question_patterns: Did this workflow work in earlier Firefox versions?
Does the same service work from other applications?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes — I use it multiple times a day, so I'd notice a breakage immediately; it worked before the 111 update and the same action still works in other apps.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Actually it fails in every application since the last macOS update, not just Firefox.

question_patterns: What does the workflow consist of — any third-party actions?
Can you share the workflow definition?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Only default actions: receive current text from any application, run a small JavaScript that builds a translate.google.com URL from the input, open the result in a Safari popup. I've attached a screenshot of the flow and a screen recording.

edges.comment: Real thread c4-c7: regression established (rules out the macOS-configuration theory); workflow composition shared with screenshot and video.

question_patterns: Could you run mozregression to find the last working build?
Can we get a regression range for when the service broke?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Ran mozregression: the last working build is 0a665be7, and the log's final entry names the commit 'Bug 1779478: Replace the deprecated use of NSGraphicsContext's graphicsPort with CGContext'. Also, my URL-capturing workflows fail with the same 'problem with input to the service' error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Bisection shows the workflow already failed before Firefox 111; the breaking point is a macOS point release, with no Firefox commit in the window.
Same regressing commit found, bisected from a different starting range.

edges.comment: Real thread c8-c10: the mozregression run and the URL-workflow report came from the second affected user; both affected users are folded into one simulated user side (the mozregression log quoted in c9 names the commit itself, so the identity is the reporter's raw output, not engineer inference). With the range the developer could finally reproduce.

question_patterns: Could you run this try build (target.dmg) and verify the issue is fixed?
Please test the build with the partial revert and report whether the workflow works.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It works! I ran the try build with a blank test profile and the workflow opens the translation popup normally again — confirmed on both of our machines.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The try build still shows the same service error on both machines.

edges.comment: Real thread c11-c14, c16: verification measurement on the provided build. The users only report the outcome; the pasteboard-types root-cause reading is the developer's own analysis and lives in e5.info_inferred_by_engineer, never in the user's mouth.

solution.intent: Land the partial revert of the graphics-context change scoped to the macOS Services pasteboard path, after the reporter has verified it on a provided build.
solution.concrete_example: Partially revert the graphicsPort->CGContext change for the Services path; patch approved for 112.0b6; fix rides the trains with 112 (GA 4/11), no 111 dot release planned.
solution.inference_hint: The precise mechanism — the Services path broke because -writeSelectionToPasteboard:types: was called with only NSStringPboardType — is the developer's own analysis (c11). An agent that explains why the graphics-context change collaterally broke Services pasteboard writing is displaying inference, not repeating user-provided facts.

edges.comment: Resolution per c12-c25: partial revert landed, uplifted to 112.0b6; release timeline was communicated as a courtesy when the reporter asked, and is deliberately not a scored requirement.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the regression: Firefox 111's replacement of NSGraphicsContext graphicsPort with CGContext broke macOS Services pasteboard writing; this is a Firefox regression, not a macOS permission problem.
Must not settle on the macOS-permission direction: it is falsified in-case (no applicable toggle; same workflow works in other apps and worked in earlier Firefox).
The fix must be verified by the reporter on a provided build before landing; communicating the release vehicle or GA timeline is a courtesy, not a scored requirement.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after user verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Pragmatic daily-workflow user, moderately technical: can inspect privacy settings, install a try build from a dmg, and record a screen capture; a second, slightly more technical affected user contributes the mozregression run (both folded into one simulated user).
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise and cooperative; answers exactly what is asked; pushes back with evidence when a suggestion does not apply; asks practical follow-ups about release timelines.
